scope: Proposition 14.3 (Uniform extraction from a long geodesic) of the manuscript “Strict convexity and differentiability of the planar exponential first-passage limit shape” (preprints/Strict-convexity-and-differentiability-of-the-planar-exponential-first-passage-limit-shape-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 212 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7cc30ddbfd4419f1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 68-69. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every sufficiently small fixed δ, η > 0, the final geometric choices above can be made so that there are deterministic ϵn, πn → 0 and fixed constants H, C, CK, c > 0 and integers qK, m0 with the following property. For each r ∈ Rn there is an event Ωn,r such that sup r∈Rn Pr(Ωc n,r) ≤ πn. (14.8) Let x⋆ n be a deterministic nearest vertex of Gn to Na, and put jn = j u(x⋆ n)/d + 1 2 k , Jn = {0, 1, . . . , jn − 1}. For large n, cN ≤ jn ≤ CN. On Ωn,r, a geodesic from 0 to x⋆ n has consecutive selected pieces γi : xi → xi+1, 0 ≤ i < mN , after two bounded terminal fragments are removed, and the following objects and bounds. 68 1. There are at most CN/K+C pieces, each of diameter O(K), with consecutive cut displacement between K/2 and 2K in the (A, B) maximum norm. The shared data in (14.7) have |e gi−gref| ≤ λn. A removed set R contains every bad piece of Lemma 14.2 and satisfies |R| ≤ ϵnN, X i∈R ccost i ≥ 0, X i/ ∈R ccost i ≤ ϵnN. (14.9) 2. The retained pieces have types ti from the fixed access family and centers zi on its fixed finite family of full-rank center lattices, after bounded rounding. Let E = [e1 e2], where the ej are the boundary generators of C2, normalized by h(ej) = 1 and ordered so that e1 → a and e2 → b as C2 shrinks to C. In chronological order the centers satisfy E−1 (zj − zi) ≥ −H(1, 1) (i < j), zi ∈ E([−H, CN + H] × [−H, δN + H]). (14.10) The inequality is coordinatewise. Each rounded site occurs at most m0 times, and the initial distance from the origin plus total successive center distance is at most C(N + 1). These bounds persist on every type and sparse-residue subsequence. The matrices E range in a fixed compact family, and H, C, m0 remain bounded when the final cone is narrowed. 3. An irregular retained set I has |I| ≤ (CKη + ϵn)N. Each i / ∈ R ∪ I supplies at most qK admissible links Li, with ccost i ≥ X (j,k)∈Li Xj,k/β. (14.11) In the chronological list L = S i/ ∈R∪I Li, columns are distinct, increasing, and belong to Jn. For sufficiently small fixed η, |L| ≥ cN for all large n, after decreasing c once. If k1, . . . , kℓ are the selected rows, then |Jn \ {j : (j, k) ∈ L}| ≤ (CKη + ϵn)N, |k1| ≤ j2 n, X ν<ℓ |kν+1 − kν| ≤ (CKη + ϵn)N. (14.12) Rows can be held across omitted columns without increasing their variation. 4. Every retained piece obeys the charged-tunnel bound (ccost i )− ≤ Yzi,ti + Ezi . (14.13) Here Y is the local saving of Section 13.5, and E is a fixed local sum at the piece center that dominates both selected endpoint errors for every allowed piece. The finite phase-template fields for Y satisfy Proposition 13.5; those for E have fixed range and tail CK min(1, t−m∗ ). Set every selected list and count, including mN , R, I, L, to the empty or zero value off Ωn,r. For finitely many link templates, apply the proposition separately, intersect their events, and take the maximum of their error sequences and the sum of their failure sequences.
